where: Section 2, average-current method (paragraph and table row)
problem: The claim that the nMOS 'stays in saturation' over the whole VDD-to-VDD/2 swing is wrong. The nMOS is saturated only while Vout > VDD − Vtn. With Vtn < VDD/2 (the normal case, e.g. 0.5 V against 1.8 V) it leaves saturation at Vout = 1.3 V, above the 50% point of 0.9 V, and spends the lower part of the swing in the linear region with a smaller current. So the formula is not derived from a saturation current over the half swing; it is an optimistic estimate.
fix: Say: 'The nMOS is saturated only until the output falls to VDD − Vtn; below that it enters the linear region and its current drops. Using the saturation current for the whole half swing gives a simple, optimistic estimate of tPHL; the real delay is somewhat longer.' Make the table assumption read 'device current approximated by IDsat over the half swing (optimistic)'.

problem: 'The output holds its old value until the input passes the switching threshold, then falls' is wrong. The output starts to fall once the rising input passes Vtn (about 0.5 V here), well before Vin reaches VDD/2 at 2 ns. Only the 50% crossings are used to define tPHL; they do not mark the start of the fall.
fix: 'The output begins to fall as soon as the input passes Vtn; it crosses VDD/2 at 2.5 ns, 0.5 ns after the input crossed VDD/2. That 0.5 ns interval is tPHL.' (The digital bar chart may still snap at the 50% points, but the caption must say so.)

where: Section 1, paragraph on rise time versus delay
problem: The example 'a short tp and a long tr if its driver is weak but the threshold is crossed early' is self-contradictory: a weak driver crosses 50% late, not early. For a single exponential tr ≈ 3.2 tp, so the two are not independent in the way stated.
fix: Give a real case instead: a node with a weak resistive pull-up crosses 50% quickly and then crawls to VDD, so tr can be much more than 3 times tp; tr describes the whole edge shape, tp only the time to the 50% crossing.

where: Worked example 1, steps 1-6 and Section 2 RC paragraph
problem: Superscripts are lost in the plain-text steps: '2.66×10−10 s', '(200×10−6/2)', '100×10−6', and 'e−t/τ'. A student reading 'VDD(1 − e−t/τ)' can misread it as e minus t over τ.

Req ≈ VDD/(2·IDsat) combined with tp = 0.69 Req CL gives 0.345 CLVDD/IDsat, while the average-current formula gives 0.5 CLVDD/IDsat — about 30% apart for the same device, and the text does not say the two methods are not numerically identical.
fix: Add one line: 'The two estimates differ by about 30% because one averages the current and the other fixes a single equivalent resistance; both are hand estimates, and the simulation is the reference.'

problem: 'Cgd gives a short feedthrough spike at the output ... which is why a floating output node is never left undriven' draws a weak causal link. Floating nodes are mainly avoided because of charge sharing, leakage and noise, not because of the Cgd spike.
fix: Keep the two ideas separate: the Miller term explains the extra input load; the feedthrough spike explains glitches on a dynamic node. Give the real reason for never leaving an output floating (leakage and charge sharing make its level undefined).

problem: 'the four standard numbers (tPHL, tPLH, tp, and rise/fall times)' lists five quantities under the count of four.
fix: 'the standard numbers (tPHL, tPLH, tp, tr and tf)'.
